779:   const sendMessage = useCallback(
780:     async (
781:       text: string,
782:       attachments: ChatAttachmentPayload[] = [],
783:       options: { from?: string } = {},
784:     ) => {
785:       const trimmed = text.trim();
786:       if ((!trimmed && !attachments.length) || streaming) {
787:         return;
788:       }
789: 
790:       // A re-ask replaces the turn it starts from: the old question and the
791:       // answer it got are the same turn, and keeping both would read as a
792:       // conversation the reader never had.
793:       const cut = options.from
794:         ? messages.findIndex((message) => message.id === options.from)
795:         : -1;
796:       const replaced = cut >= 0 ? messages.slice(0, cut) : messages;
797: 
798:       // Files ride only on the newest turn. Re-sending megabytes of base64 with
799:       // every later question would make each turn slower than the last.
800:       const history: ChatMessage[] = [
801:         ...replaced.map((message) =>
802:           message.attachments
803:             ? {
804:                 id: message.id,
805:                 role: message.role,
806:                 content: message.content,
807:                 parts: message.parts,
808:               }
809:             : message,
810:         ),
811:         {
812:           role: "user",
813:           id: newTurnId(),
814:           content: trimmed,
815:           ...(attachments.length ? { attachments } : {}),
816:         },
817:       ];
818:       const assistantIndex = history.length;
819:       const assistantId = newTurnId();
820:       setMessages([
821:         ...history,
822:         { role: "assistant", id: assistantId, content: "", parts: [] },
823:       ]);
824:       setStreaming(true);
825:       setThinkingPhase("health_check");
826:       setOfflineReply(false);
827: 
828:       const controller = new AbortController();
829:       abortRef.current = controller;
830: 
831:       let content = "";
832:       let parts: ChatPart[] = [];
833:       let steps: RunStep[] = [];
834:       let failure: StudioError | null = null;
835:       let terminal = false;
836:       let stopped = false;
837: 
838:       // Prose is appended to the open text part; a surface opens a new one, so
839:       // the transcript keeps the agent's order instead of gathering all prose
840:       // above all cards.
841:       const appendText = (text: string) => {
842:         if (!text) {
843:           return;
844:         }
845:         content += text;
846:         const last = parts[parts.length - 1];
847:         parts =
848:           last?.kind === "text"
849:             ? [...parts.slice(0, -1), { kind: "text", text: last.text + text }]
850:             : [...parts, { kind: "text", text }];
851:       };
852: 
853:       // The turn owns its own timeline, so a finished run stays inspectable and
854:       // the next turn starts from nothing without a reset elsewhere.
855:       const publish = () => {
856:         setMessages((prev) => {
857:           if (prev.length <= assistantIndex) {
858:             return prev;
859:           }
860:           const next = [...prev];
861:           next[assistantIndex] = {
862:             role: "assistant",
863:             id: assistantId,
864:             content,
865:             parts: [...parts],
866:             ...(failure ? { error: failure, retryText: trimmed } : {}),
867:             ...(stopped ? { stopped: true, retryText: trimmed } : {}),
868:             ...(failure || stopped
869:               ? attachments.length
870:                 ? { retryAttachments: attachments }
871:                 : {}
872:               : {}),
873:             ...(steps.length ? { tools: [...steps] } : {}),
874:           };
875:           return next;
876:         });
877:       };
878: 
879:       const handleEvent = (event: RawSseEvent) => {
880:         switch (event.event) {
881:           case "status": {
882:             const phase = String(event.data.phase ?? "");
883:             setThinkingPhase(phase);
884:             if (phase === "offline") {
885:               setOfflineReply(true);
886:             }
887:             break;
888:           }
889:           case "delta": {
890:             appendText(String(event.data.text ?? ""));
891:             publish();
892:             break;
893:           }
894:           case "ui": {
895:             // Validate again on arrival: the connection is local but the
896:             // renderer must never trust a shape it has not checked.
897:             const parsed = parseUiSpec(event.data.spec, catalogManifest());
898:             if (parsed.ok) {
899:               parts = [
900:                 ...parts,
901:                 { kind: "ui", id: String(event.data.id ?? `ui-${parts.length}`), node: parsed.node },
902:               ];
903:               publish();
904:             }
905:             break;
906:           }
907:           case "tool":
908:             steps = applyToolEvent(
909:               steps,
910:               {
911:                 name: String(event.data.name ?? ""),
912:                 status: String(event.data.status ?? ""),
913:                 preview: event.data.preview ? String(event.data.preview) : undefined,
914:               },
915:               Date.now(),
916:             );
917:             publish();
918:             break;
919:           case "message": {
920:             terminal = true;
921:             content = String(event.data.content ?? content);
922:             const hasSurfaces = parts.some((part) => part.kind === "ui");
923:             if (!hasSurfaces) {
924:               parts = content ? [{ kind: "text", text: content }] : [];
925:             }
926:             publish();
927:             break;
928:           }
929:           case "conversation": {
930:             const id = String(event.data.id ?? "");
931:             if (id) {
932:               setConversationId(id);
933:             }
934:             break;
935:           }
936:           case "memory": {
937:             const observation = event.data.observation as Observation | undefined;
938:             if (observation?.id) {
939:               setMemory((prev) =>
940:                 prev.some((item) => item.id === observation.id)
941:                   ? prev.map((item) => (item.id === observation.id ? observation : item))
942:                   : [...prev, observation],
943:               );
944:             }
945:             break;
946:           }
947:           case "canvas_dirty":
948:             void refreshCanvas();
949:             break;
950:           case "connector": {
951:             if (String(event.data.status ?? "") === "error") {
952:               const reason = String(event.data.error ?? "The connector could not be added.");
953:               setMessages((prev) => [
954:                 ...prev,
955:                 { role: "notice", id: newTurnId(), content: `Connector failed: ${reason}` },
956:               ]);
957:             } else {
958:               setConnectorSuggestions((prev) => {
959:                 const id = String(event.data?.preset ?? event.data?.name ?? "");
960:                 if (!id || prev.includes(id)) {
961:                   return prev;
962:                 }
963:                 return [...prev, id];
964:               });
965:             }
966:             void refreshConnectors();
967:             break;
968:           }
969:           case "error": {
970:             terminal = true;
971:             failure = readStudioError(event.data.error);
972:             publish();
973:             break;
974:           }
975:           default:
976:             break;
977:         }
978:       };
979: 
980:       try {
981:         await streamChat(
982:           {
983:             base_url: settings.base_url,
984:             api_key: settings.api_key,
985:             model: settings.model_name,
986:             mcp_url: settings.mcp_url,
987:             messages: history,
988:             brief,
989:             ui_catalog: catalogManifest(),
990:             conversation_id: conversationId,
991:           },
992:           handleEvent,
993:           controller.signal,
994:         );
995:       } catch (error) {
996:         const aborted = (error as Error).name === "AbortError";
997:         if (aborted) {
998:           // An abort is the user's own doing, so it is not a failure — but it is
999:           // still a fact about the turn. Keep what arrived, stop any tool that
1000:           // was mid-flight, and leave the turn in place so the transcript says
1001:           // what happened instead of silently losing the question.
1002:           stopped = true;
1003:           steps = steps.map((step) =>
1004:             step.status === "running"
1005:               ? {
1006:                   ...step,
1007:                   status: "stopped",
1008:                   preview: step.preview ?? "Stopped before it returned.",
1009:                   endedAt: Date.now(),
1010:                 }
1011:               : step,
1012:           );
1013:           publish();
1014:         } else {
1015:           terminal = true;
1016:           failure = asStudioError(error);
1017:           publish();
1018:         }
1019:       } finally {
1020:         if (!terminal && !failure && !stopped) {
1021:           // The stream ended without a message or an error: something failed
1022:           // silently, and the user must still be told.
1023:           failure = {
1024:             code: "internal",
1025:             message: "The assistant stopped before answering.",
1026:             suggestion: "Try again — your question is still here.",
1027:             retryable: true,
1028:           };
1029:           publish();
1030:         }
1031:         setStreaming(false);
1032:         setThinkingPhase(null);
1033:         abortRef.current = null;
1034:       }
1035:     },
1036:     [
1037:       messages,
1038:       streaming,
1039:       settings,
1040:       brief,
1041:       conversationId,
1042:       refreshCanvas,
1043:       refreshConnectors,
1044:     ],

106:  * A `start` opens a step; `ok`/`error` resolves the newest open step with that
107:  * name. A result with no matching start (a replayed stream, a client that
108:  * joined late) becomes a finished step rather than being dropped.
109:  */
110: export function applyToolEvent(steps: RunStep[], event: ToolEvent, now: number): RunStep[] {
111:   const name = event.name.trim() || "tool";
112: 
113:   if (event.status === "start") {
114:     return [
115:       ...steps,
116:       {
117:         id: `${name}-${steps.length}`,
118:         name,
119:         status: "running",
120:         startedAt: now,
121:       },
122:     ];
123:   }
124: 
125:   const status: RunStepStatus = event.status === "error" ? "error" : "ok";
126:   const open = lastOpenStep(steps, name);
127:   if (open === -1) {
128:     return [
129:       ...steps,
130:       {
131:         id: `${name}-${steps.length}`,
132:         name,
133:         status,
134:         preview: event.preview,
135:         startedAt: now,
136:         endedAt: now,
137:       },
138:     ];
139:   }
140: 
141:   return steps.map((step, index) =>
142:     index === open
143:       ? { ...step, status, preview: event.preview ?? step.preview, endedAt: now }
144:       : step,
145:   );
146: }
147: 
148: /** Durations are read at a glance, so they stay to one short form. */
149: export function formatDuration(ms: number): string {
150:   if (!Number.isFinite(ms) || ms < 0) {
151:     return "0s";
152:   }
153:   if (ms < 1000) {
154:     return `${(ms / 1000).toFixed(1)}s`;
155:   }
156:   if (ms < 60_000) {
157:     const seconds = ms / 1000;
158:     return `${seconds < 10 ? seconds.toFixed(1) : Math.round(seconds)}s`;
159:   }
160:   const minutes = Math.floor(ms / 60_000);
161:   const seconds = Math.round((ms % 60_000) / 1000);
162:   return `${minutes}m ${seconds}s`;
163: }
164: 
165: /** The step still in flight, if the run has one. */
166: export function runningStep(steps: RunStep[]): RunStep | null {
167:   for (let index = steps.length - 1; index >= 0; index -= 1) {
168:     if (steps[index].status === "running") {
169:       return steps[index];
170:     }
171:   }
172:   return null;
173: }
174: 
175: /**
176:  * What the studio is doing right now: the tool it is waiting on, or the phase
177:  * it is in. Deliberately about work, never about the model's reasoning.
178:  */
179: export function activityLabel(phase: string | null, steps: RunStep[]): string {
180:   const running = runningStep(steps);
181:   if (running) {
182:     return stepLabel(running.name);
183:   }
184:   return (phase ? PHASE_LABELS[phase] : undefined) ?? "Thinking";
185: }
186: 
187: /**
188:  * The one line a finished run leaves behind. Counts and time only: the point is
189:  * that work happened, not a replay of every call.
190:  */
191: export function runSummary(steps: RunStep[], now: number): string {
192:   if (!steps.length) {
193:     return "";
194:   }
195:   const started = Math.min(...steps.map((step) => step.startedAt));
196:   const ended = Math.max(...steps.map((step) => step.endedAt ?? now));
197:   const failures = steps.filter((step) => step.status === "error").length;
198:   const parts = [`${steps.length} tool${steps.length === 1 ? "" : "s"}`];
199:   if (failures) {
200:     parts.push(`${failures} failed`);
201:   }
202:   parts.push(formatDuration(ended - started));
203:   return parts.join(" · ");
204: }

Now I see the big picture. The `integrate-assistant-ui` branch had a much richer `convert.ts` that handles:
- `reasoning` parts (chain of thought)
- `ui` parts as data-* surfaces
- `source` parts (references)
- `tool` parts with approval flows (tool-call with approval)
- `toChatMessage` (inverse conversion)

The `attachments.ts` had `createAttachmentAdapter` and `preparedAttachments` for handling file uploads through assistant-ui's attachment system.

Our branch (`ui-not-looking-like-shit`) took a simplified approach:
- Moved conversion to `lib/thread.ts` with simpler functions (`toThreadMessage`, `textOf`, `turnFromAppend`, `metaOf`)
- Removed the `StudioRuntime.tsx` provider and inlined the runtime into `Conversation.tsx`
- Removed `attachments.ts` (attachments are handled directly in `ChatStage.tsx` and `StudioContext.tsx`)
- Removed the `toChatMessage` inverse conversion
- Removed tool approval handling (`onRespondToToolApproval`, `respondToApproval`)

Our branch (`ui-not-looking-like-shit`) has a simpler, more self-contained approach:
- Runtime embedded in `Conversation.tsx`
- Simpler `ChatPart` (just `text` and `ui`)
- Attachments handled through `ChatStage.tsx` directly calling `sendMessage(text, attachments)`
- No reasoning, source, or tool approval support

parts.text:
This is very revealing. The `feat/studio-assistant-ui-experience` branch represents a significant evolution of the assistant-ui integration. It includes:

**Backend changes (studio-api):**
1. New `approvals.py` module - for tool approval flows
2. `chat.py` changes:
   - `MUTATING_TOOL_PREFIXES` - identifies tools that need approval
   - `is_mutating_tool()` - check function
   - `MAX_ATTACHMENTS`, `MAX_ATTACHMENT_TEXT`, `MAX_SOURCE_PREVIEW`
   - Tool approval flow with `wait_for_decision`
   - Source references (provenance chips)
   - Attachment refs instead of embedded base64
3. `schemas.py` changes:
   - `ChatAttachment` → `AttachmentRef` (client-side file handling, text extraction by client)
   - `ChatRequest` has `approvals`, `assistant_id` fields
   - `ApprovalDecisionRequest`/`ApprovalDecisionResponse`
   - `TurnNode` for conversation tree (branching)
   - `ConversationModel` has `head_id` for branch positioning
   - `TurnModel` has `message_id`, `parent_id`
   - `ConversationTreeResponse` - full branch tree
   - `UpdateConversationRequest` - for updating head_id

**Frontend changes (studio):**
1. `StudioRuntime.tsx` - Full provider with all handlers
2. `convert.ts` - Bidirectional conversion with reasoning, sources, tool approvals
3. `parts.tsx` - Part renderers using assistant-ui's scoped state
4. `ThreadComposer.tsx` and `composerParts.tsx` - Assistant-ui composer
5. `attachments.ts` - Attachment adapter for assistant-ui

**Our branch (`ui-not-looking-like-shit`) has:**
1. Simplified `Conversation.tsx` with inlined runtime
2. `lib/thread.ts` with simplified conversion (no reasoning, sources, tool approvals)
3. `ChatStage.tsx` handles attachments directly
4. No branching, no tool approvals

So the "crash" seems to be that our branch was an earlier, simpler attempt at the assistant-ui integration, and the `feat/studio-assistant-ui-experience` branch represents the more complete "max" version.

Now, the user wants us to "pick up from where we left off" to "ensure assistant-ui is installed and used to the max." This means we need to bring the full assistant-ui capabilities from `feat/studio-assistant-ui-experience` into our branch.

But wait - the user said "we had a crash" and we need to "pick up from where we left off on this topic branch." This suggests our branch IS the current state of work, and we need to continue building on it.

Let me also check what the `fix/assistant-ui-turn-context` branch has - it's a fix for "preserve assistant-ui turn context."

"""In-process approval gates for mutating tool calls.

A mutating MCP tool (``add_job``, ``update_outcome``, …) pauses the streaming
turn until the person in front of the Studio says yes or no. The gate is a
process-local registry of pending futures: the SSE generator awaits one, and
``POST /api/approvals/{id}`` resolves it.

This is deliberately the smallest thing that is honest. The sidecar serves one
local user over one loopback socket; it has no durable job state and no worker
pool, so a gate that lives in memory is the whole requirement. Every gate has a
timeout and every gate resolves once, so a turn can never hang and a double
click can never run a tool twice.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import threading
import uuid
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timezone

#: A person deciding whether the agent may write to their data deserves longer
#: than a network timeout, but the turn must still end on its own.
DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300.0


@dataclass
class ApprovalRequest:
    """One pending decision, described well enough for the UI to ask."""

    id: str
    tool_call_id: str
    name: str
    arguments: dict[str, object]
    prompt: str
    created_at: str = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat())

    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        return {
            "id": self.id,
            "tool_call_id": self.tool_call_id,
            "name": self.name,
            "arguments": self.arguments,
            "prompt": self.prompt,
            "created_at": self.created_at,
        }


@dataclass
class ApprovalDecision:
    approved: bool
    reason: str = ""


class ApprovalNotFoundError(KeyError):
    """No pending gate has that id, or it already resolved."""


class ApprovalRegistry:
    """Pending approval gates, keyed by the id the client answers with."""

    def __init__(self) -> None:
        self._lock = threading.Lock()
        self._pending: dict[str, asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision]] = {}

    def open(
        self,
        *,
        tool_call_id: str,
        name: str,
        arguments: dict[str, object],
        prompt: str,
    ) -> tuple[ApprovalRequest, asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision]]:
        """Register a gate and return its description and the future to await."""
        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
        request = ApprovalRequest(
            id=f"apv_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}",
            tool_call_id=tool_call_id,
            name=name,
            arguments=arguments,
            prompt=prompt,
        )
        future: asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision] = loop.create_future()
        with self._lock:
            self._pending[request.id] = future
        return request, future

    def resolve(self, approval_id: str, decision: ApprovalDecision) -> None:
        """Answer a pending gate. Raises when the gate is unknown or already closed."""
        with self._lock:
            future = self._pending.pop(approval_id, None)
        if future is None or future.done():
            raise ApprovalNotFoundError(approval_id)
        future.set_result(decision)

    def discard(self, approval_id: str) -> None:
        """Forget a gate without answering it (the turn ended first)."""
        with self._lock:
            self._pending.pop(approval_id, None)

    def cancel_all(self) -> None:
        """Drop every pending gate. Called when the sidecar shuts down."""
        with self._lock:
            pending = list(self._pending.items())
            self._pending.clear()
        for _approval_id, future in pending:
            if not future.done():
                future.cancel()

    @property
    def pending(self) -> int:
        with self._lock:
            return len(self._pending)


async def wait_for_decision(
    registry: ApprovalRegistry,
    request: ApprovalRequest,
    future: asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision],
    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
) -> ApprovalDecision | None:
    """Await a decision, returning ``None`` when the gate expired or was dropped.

    The gate is always discarded, so an expired id can never be answered later
    and a cancelled turn leaves nothing behind.
    """
    try:
        return await asyncio.wait_for(future, timeout=timeout)
    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
        return None
    except asyncio.CancelledError:
        raise
    finally:
        registry.discard(request.id)


__all__ = [
    "ApprovalDecision",
    "ApprovalNotFoundError",
    "ApprovalRegistry",
    "ApprovalRequest",
    "DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS",
    "wait_for_decision",
]

2. **Tool approvals** - `ApprovalRegistry`, `wait_for_decision`, mutating tool detection, `"approval"` SSE events
3. **Source frames** - `_source_frame()` and `"source"` SSE events for provenance
4. **Branching support** - `assistant_id`, `parent_id`, `message_id` in schemas
5. **Attachment changes** - `AttachmentRef` instead of `ChatAttachmentPayload`, client-side text extraction
6. **Conversation tree endpoints** - `ConversationTreeResponse`, `TurnNode`

And the frontend changes include:
1. **StudioRuntime.tsx** - Full provider with all handlers
2. **convert.ts** - Rich bidirectional conversion
3. **parts.tsx** - Part renderers with reasoning, sources, tool approvals
4. **attachments.ts** - Attachment adapter
5. **ThreadComposer.tsx** - Using `ComposerPrimitive`
6. **Conversation.tsx** - Using `MessagePrimitive`, `BranchPickerPrimitive`

1: """Conversational helper with offline fallbacks and a streaming tool loop.
2: 
3: The loop fans the MCP tools and three local tools — ``render_ui``,
4: ``remember``, and ``add_connector`` — into the completion. Local tools are
5: intercepted rather than forwarded: ``render_ui`` validates its spec against the
6: catalog the client sent and streams a ``ui`` event, ``remember`` stores a
7: suggested observation and streams a ``memory`` event, and ``add_connector``
8: writes the shared connector registry and streams a ``connector`` event.
9: 
10: The conversation is persisted when a memory store is supplied, so a PM can leave
11: and come back to the same thread and the same working context.
12: """
13:

48: SYSTEM_PROMPT = """You are an elite product strategist working inside The Living Studio, a room built for product managers.
49: Your job is to help the PM choose and win the next opportunity that matters — to customers, the business, and their career.
50: Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI) is your private engine, not the conversation. Translate the PM's ambition into jobs, outcomes, and evidence silently, and speak in the PM's language.
51: 
52: How to work:
53: 1. Start with the person and the stakes. Ask what opportunity they are chasing, who it is for, and what winning would change. One good question at a time.
54: 2. Mirror their words back, then offer a sharp hypothesis they can correct.
55: 3. When they give you context worth keeping — a career goal, a constraint, a stakeholder, a belief — call `remember` with the smallest useful observation. Do not ask permission first; the UI lets them confirm, edit, or dismiss it.
56: 4. Use ODI when it earns its keep: a job statement clarifies, a desired outcome sharpens, an opportunity score compares. Never lead with the framework or lecture about stages.
57: 5. Opportunity Score = Importance + max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0). Above 10 means underserved.
58: 6. When a surface carries the evidence better than a paragraph, call `render_ui` once, then write one short sentence. Never describe in prose what a card can already show.
59: 7. The conversation is the product: every surface you render lands in the thread the PM is already reading. Never tell them to open a panel, a tab, or a view to see something you can show inline.
60: 8. Capture and simulation are conversations, not forms: ask for the customer's words or the bet in plain language, render the card that carries it, and offer the next move as an action on that card.
61: 9. When asked to add or query Jobs, Steps, or Outcomes, ALWAYS invoke the corresponding tools.
62: 10. Be warm, direct, and specific. Short sentences. No corporate jargon, no therapy-speak, no emojis."""
63:

65: def _brief_lines(brief: StudioBrief | None) -> list[str]:
66:     if brief is None:
67:         return []
68:     facts = [
69:         ("Product", brief.product_name),
70:         ("Product URL", brief.product_url),
71:         ("Who it serves", brief.target_user),
72:         ("Job to be done", brief.job_statement),
73:         ("Core problem", brief.core_problem),
74:     ]
75:     return [f"- {label}: {value}" for label, value in facts if value.strip()]
76:

78: def _brief_block(brief: StudioBrief | None) -> str:
79:     lines = _brief_lines(brief)
80:     if not lines:
81:         return ""
82:     return (
83:         "\n\nThe user set this context during onboarding. Treat it as given and do not "
84:         "re-ask for it:\n" + "\n".join(lines)

88: def offline_fallback(user_input: str, brief: StudioBrief | None = None) -> str:
89:     """Deterministic, honest guidance when no LLM backend is reachable.
90: 
91:     No fabricated customer data, no invented scores: the studio says what it can
92:     do by hand and points at the surface that does it.
93:     """
94:     lower_inp = user_input.lower()
95:     context = ""
96:     if brief is not None and brief.job_statement.strip():
97:         context = (
98:             f"\n\n**Working job:** {brief.job_statement.strip()}"
99:             if not brief.product_name.strip()
100:             else f"\n\n**{brief.product_name.strip()}** — {brief.job_statement.strip()}"
101:         )
102: 
103:     if "guideline" in lower_inp or "framework" in lower_inp or "stage" in lower_inp:
104:         return (
105:             "### ODI, stage by stage\n\n"
106:             "1. **Define the job** — the functional progress a person is trying to make.\n"
107:             "2. **Capture desired outcomes** — `[direction] + [unit of measure] + [object of control] + [context]`.\n"
108:             "3. **Score the opportunity** — `importance + max(importance - satisfaction, 0)`; above 10 is underserved.\n"
109:             "4. **Map the job** — Define, Locate, Prepare, Confirm, Execute, Monitor, Modify, Conclude.\n\n"
110:             "Type `/capture` to record an outcome, `/jobmap` to walk the phases, "
111:             "and `/landscape` to see what is underserved." + context
112:         )
113:     if "simulate" in lower_inp or "bet" in lower_inp or "impact" in lower_inp:
114:         return (
115:             "### Simulate the bet by hand\n\n"
116:             "Open **`/impact`** and pick the outcome you want to test. The simulation "
117:             "shows before/after friction; it no longer invents a result when no model "
118:             "is connected." + context
119:         )
120:     if "evidence" in lower_inp or "call" in lower_inp or "quote" in lower_inp:
121:         return (
122:             "### Evidence needs a source\n\n"
123:             "No connector is wired up, so there is no live transcript to quote. "
124:             "Capture the signal you already have in **`/capture`** — the evidence field "
125:             "is stored with the outcome." + context
126:         )
127:     return (
128:         "I can't reason about that right now — no model is reachable. "
129:         "The studio still works by hand:\n\n"
130:         "- `/start` — set or correct your context\n"
131:         "- `/capture` — record an outcome with importance and satisfaction\n"
132:         "- `/jobmap` — add or edit the steps of the job\n"
133:         "- `/landscape` — review what is underserved\n\n"
134:         "Type `/help` for every command, or point Settings at a local model to "
135:         "bring the assistant back." + context
136:     )

140:     return f"event: {event}\ndata: {json.dumps(data)}\n\n"

143: class _TurnFailure(Exception):
144:     """A fatal failure that ends the turn with one ``error`` event."""
145: 
146:     def __init__(self, error: StudioError) -> None:
147:         self.error = error

151: def _error_frame(problem: StudioError, request_id: str) -> str:
152:     """Render the terminal ``error`` event for a fatal turn failure."""
153:     body = problem.model_copy(update={"request_id": request_id or problem.request_id})
154:     return _sse("error", {"error": body.model_dump(mode="json"), "request_id": request_id})

157: #: Base64 adds a third to the payload, and every round of a turn carries it, so
158: #: one turn must not be able to become an unbounded upload.
159: MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024
160: 
161: #: Text is inlined whole only up to this much. Past it the model is told the file
162: #: was cut, instead of being handed a truncated quote as if it were complete.
163: MAX_INLINE_CHARS = 120_000
164: 
165: #: Text-bearing media types whose payload is safe to inline as prose.
166: INLINE_MEDIA_TYPES = {
167:     "application/json",
168:     "application/xml",
169:     "application/yaml",
170:     "application/x-yaml",
171:     "application/toml",
172:     "application/csv",
173:     "application/x-ndjson",
174:     "application/sql",
175: }

178: def _media_type(attachment: ChatAttachment) -> str:
179:     return (attachment.media_type or "").split(";")[0].strip().lower()
180: 
181: 
182: def _attachment_bytes(attachment: ChatAttachment) -> bytes:
183:     return base64.b64decode(attachment.data, validate=True)
184:

186: def _attachment_problem(attachment: ChatAttachment) -> str | None:
187:     """Why this file cannot be read, or None when it can.
188: 
189:     A file the model cannot open is refused instead of being mentioned as if it
190:     had been read: a filename is not evidence.
191:     """
192:     media = _media_type(attachment)
193:     readable = media.startswith("image/") or media.startswith("text/")
194:     if not media:
195:         return "has no media type"
196:     if not readable and media not in INLINE_MEDIA_TYPES:
197:         return f"is a {media} file, which the model cannot read"
198:     try:
199:         raw = _attachment_bytes(attachment)
200:     except (binascii.Error, ValueError):
201:         return "is not valid base64"
202:     if not raw:
203:         return "is empty"
204:     if len(raw) > MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES:
205:         return f"is larger than {MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES // (1024 * 1024)} MB"
206:     if not media.startswith("image/"):
207:         try:
208:             raw.decode("utf-8")
209:         except UnicodeDecodeError:
210:             return "is not UTF-8 text"
211:     return None
212:

214: def _attachment_part(attachment: ChatAttachment) -> dict[str, Any]:
215:     """One OpenAI content part: an image, or a text file inlined verbatim."""
216:     media = _media_type(attachment)
217:     if media.startswith("image/"):
218:         return {
219:             "type": "image_url",
220:             "image_url": {"url": f"data:{media};base64,{attachment.data}"},
221:         }
222:     text = _attachment_bytes(attachment).decode("utf-8")
223:     if len(text) > MAX_INLINE_CHARS:
224:         text = text[:MAX_INLINE_CHARS] + f"\n\n[truncated at {MAX_INLINE_CHARS} characters]"
225:     label = attachment.name or "attached file"
226:     return {"type": "text", "text": f"[{label}]\n{text}"}

229: def _message_dict(message: ChatMessage) -> dict[str, Any]:
230:     if message.role != "user" or not message.attachments:
231:         return {"role": message.role, "content": message.content}
232:     parts: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
233:     if message.content:
234:         parts.append({"type": "text", "text": message.content})
235:     parts.extend(_attachment_part(attachment) for attachment in message.attachments)
236:     return {"role": "user", "content": parts}

239: def _stored_user_text(message: ChatMessage | None) -> str:
240:     """The user's turn as the thread remembers it.
241: 
242:     The files themselves are not stored, but their names are, so a resumed
243:     conversation does not read as if the question came out of nowhere.
244:     """
245:     if message is None:
246:         return ""
247:     names = [attachment.name or "attached file" for attachment in message.attachments]
248:     if not names:
249:         return message.content
250:     return f"{message.content}\n\n[{', '.join(names)}]".strip()

257:     messages: list[dict[str, Any]] = [{"role": "system", "content": system_prompt}]
258:     messages.extend(_message_dict(message) for message in request.messages)

348: def _apply_add_connector(
349:     arguments: dict[str, Any], service: ConnectorService
350: ) -> tuple[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]:
351:     """Register a connector locally and return SSE event dicts for the stream."""
352:     name = arguments.get("name")
353:     preset_id = arguments.get("preset")
354:     url = arguments.get("url")
355:     try:
356:         config = service.add(name=name, preset_id=preset_id, url=url)
357:     except Exception as exc:  # noqa: BLE001
358:         event = {"event": "connector", "data": {"status": "error", "error": str(exc)}}
359:         return f"Error: {exc}", [event]
360:     event_data: dict[str, Any] = {"action": "registered", "name": config.name}
361:     if preset_id is not None:
362:         event_data["preset"] = preset_id
363:     if url is not None:
364:         event_data["url"] = url
365:     return f"registered connector {config.name}", [{"event": "connector", "data": event_data}]

368: def _apply_remember(
369:     arguments: dict[str, Any], memory: StudioMemory | None
370: ) -> tuple[str, dict[str, Any] | None]:
371:     """Store one suggested observation without asking the PM first."""
372:     if memory is None:
373:         return "Memory is not available to this client.", None
374: 
375:     kind = str(arguments.get("kind", ""))
376:     text = str(arguments.get("text", ""))
377:     data = arguments.get("data")
378:     try:
379:         confidence = float(arguments.get("confidence", 0.6))
380:     except (TypeError, ValueError):
381:         confidence = 0.6
382: 
383:     try:
384:         observation = memory.add_observation(
385:             kind=kind,
386:             text=text,
387:             data=data if isinstance(data, dict) else None,
388:             status="suggested",
389:             confidence=confidence,
390:         )
391:     except ValueError as exc:
392:         return f"Could not remember that: {exc}", None
393:     return "Saved for the user to review.", {"observation": observation.to_dict()}

439: def _persist_turn(
440:     memory: StudioMemory | None, conversation_id: str | None, role: str, content: str
441: ) -> None:
442:     """Record a turn, tolerating a duplicate retry and never breaking the reply."""
443:     if memory is None or conversation_id is None or not content.strip():
444:         return
445:     try:
446:         turns = memory.list_turns(conversation_id)
447:         if turns and turns[-1].role == role and turns[-1].content == content:
448:             return
449:         memory.append_turn(conversation_id, role, content)
450:     except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001
451:         return

454: async def _turn_frames(
455:     request: ChatRequest,
456:     service: ConnectorService | None,
457:     memory: StudioMemory | None,
458:     request_id: str,
459:     counters: dict[str, int],
460: ) -> AsyncIterator[str]:
461:     """Yield the frames of one turn, raising ``_TurnFailure`` on a fatal error."""
462: 
463:     def frame(event: str, data: dict[str, Any]) -> str:
464:         return _sse(event, {**data, "request_id": request_id})
465: 
466:     yield frame("status", {"phase": "health_check"})
467: 
468:     last_user_message = next(
469:         (m for m in reversed(request.messages) if m.role == "user"), None
470:     )
471:     for message in request.messages:
472:         for attachment in message.attachments:
473:             problem = _attachment_problem(attachment)
474:             if problem is not None:
475:                 raise _TurnFailure(
476:                     StudioError(
477:                         code=StudioErrorCode.VALIDATION,
478:                         message=f"{attachment.name or 'The attached file'} {problem}.",
479:                         suggestion="Attach an image or a text file, then try again.",
480:                     )
481:                 )
482: 
483:     last_user = last_user_message.content if last_user_message else ""
484: 
485:     conversation_id: str | None = None
486:     if memory is not None:
487:         conversation = (
488:             memory.get_conversation(request.conversation_id) if request.conversation_id else None
489:         )
490:         if conversation is None:
491:             conversation = memory.create_conversation()
492:         conversation_id = conversation.id
493:         _persist_turn(memory, conversation_id, "user", _stored_user_text(last_user_message))
494:         updated = memory.get_conversation(conversation_id) or conversation
495:         yield frame("conversation", {"id": updated.id, "title": updated.title})
496: 
497:     healthy, _message = await check_llm_health(request.base_url, request.api_key, request.model)
498: 
499:     if not healthy:
500:         yield frame("status", {"phase": "offline"})
501:         reply = offline_fallback(last_user, request.brief)
502:         yield frame("delta", {"text": reply})
503:         yield frame("message", {"content": reply})
504:         _persist_turn(memory, conversation_id, "assistant", reply)
505:         return
506: 
507:     catalog = UiCatalog.from_manifest(
508:         request.ui_catalog.model_dump() if request.ui_catalog else None
509:     )
510: 
511:     # The probe is a blocking socket check: keep it off the event loop.
512:     mcp_reachable = await asyncio.to_thread(is_endpoint_reachable, request.mcp_url, 0.3)
513:     if not mcp_reachable:
514:         raise _TurnFailure(
515:             StudioError(
516:                 code=StudioErrorCode.MCP_UNREACHABLE,

"""Conversational helper with offline fallbacks and a streaming tool loop.

The loop fans the MCP tools and three local tools — ``render_ui``,
``remember``, and ``add_connector`` — into the completion. Local tools are
intercepted rather than forwarded: ``render_ui`` validates its spec against the
catalog the client sent and streams a ``ui`` event, ``remember`` stores a
suggested observation and streams a ``memory`` event, and ``add_connector``
writes the shared connector registry and streams a ``connector`` event.

The conversation is persisted when a memory store is supplied, so a PM can leave
and come back to the same thread and the same working context.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import asyncio
import base64
import binascii
import json
import logging

"""Pydantic request/response contracts for the Living Studio sidecar API."""

from __future__ import annotations

from typing import Any, Literal

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field


class ChatAttachment(BaseModel):
    """One file the reader attached, as bytes the sidecar can decode.

    ``data`` is base64. Images become image content; text is inlined verbatim.
    The sidecar decides which, from ``media_type``, and refuses the rest rather
    than letting a filename stand in for content the model never saw.
    """

    name: str = ""
    media_type: str = ""
    data: str = ""


class ChatMessage(BaseModel):
    role: Literal["system", "user", "assistant", "tool"]
    content: str = ""
    attachments: list[ChatAttachment] = Field(default_factory=list)


class McpHealthRequest(BaseModel):
    mcp_url: str


class LlmHealthRequest(BaseModel):
    base_url: str
    api_key: str = ""
    model: str = ""


class ModelsRequest(BaseModel):
    base_url: str
    api_key: str = ""


class AddStepRequest(BaseModel):
    mcp_url: str
    job_id: str
    name: str
    order: int


class AddOutcomeRequest(BaseModel):
    mcp_url: str
    job_id: str
    statement: str
    importance: float
    satisfaction: float


class CreateJobRequest(BaseModel):
    """Create a Job by hand, with or without the model."""

    name: str = Field(min_length=1)
    description: str | None = None
    mcp_url: str = ""


class UpdateJobRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = None
    description: str | None = None
    mcp_url: str = ""


class UpdateStepRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = None
    order: int | None = None
    mcp_url: str = ""


class UpdateOutcomeRequest(BaseModel):
    statement: str | None = None
    importance: float | None = None
    satisfaction: float | None = None
    mcp_url: str = ""


class StudioBrief(BaseModel):
    """The user's context, captured during first-run onboarding."""

    product_name: str = ""
    product_url: str = ""
    target_user: str = ""
    job_statement: str = ""
    core_problem: str = ""


class UiCatalogRequest(BaseModel):
    """What the calling client can render. Omitted by non-visual clients."""

    version: int = 1
    components: list[dict[str, Any]] = Field(default_factory=list)


class ChatRequest(BaseModel):
    base_url: str
    api_key: str = ""
    model: str
    mcp_url: str
    messages: list[ChatMessage] = Field(default_factory=list)
    brief: StudioBrief | None = None
    ui_catalog: UiCatalogRequest | None = None
    conversation_id: str | None = None


class AddConnectorRequest(BaseModel):
    name: str | None = None
    preset: str | None = None
    url: str | None = None


class ConnectorListItem(BaseModel):
    name: str
    kind: str
    enabled: bool = True


class ConnectorOperationResponse(BaseModel):
    ok: bool
    name: str


ObservationKind = Literal[
    "career",
    "opportunity",
    "business",
    "stakeholder",
    "constraint",
    "evidence",
    "preference",
]
ObservationStatus = Literal["suggested", "confirmed", "dismissed"]


class ObservationModel(BaseModel):
    id: str
    kind: str
    text: str
    data: dict[str, Any] = Field(default_factory=dict)
    status: str
    confidence: float
    source_turn: int | None = None
    created_at: str
    updated_at: str


class ObservationListResponse(BaseModel):
    observations: list[ObservationModel]


class ObservationResponse(BaseModel):
    observation: ObservationModel


class ObservationCreateRequest(BaseModel):

1: # Agentic ODI - AI Developer Guardrails
2: 
3: This file provides system instructions and guardrails for any AI agents (or LLMs) assisting with the development of the **Agentic ODI** project. Please adhere to these guidelines to maintain consistency and align with the project's vision.
4: 
5: > **Source of Truth for ODI Methodology**: `docs/reference/Strategyn_what_is_Outcome_Driven_Innovation.pdf` by Anthony W. Ulwick (Strategyn). All ODI concepts in this project are grounded in that document. When in doubt, refer agents back to its definitions.
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 🎯 ODI Methodology Guardrails
10: 
11: This section defines how agents MUST understand and apply Outcome-Driven Innovation within this project. These are not implementation guidelines — they are domain constraints that ensure the system reflects the ODI methodology correctly.
12: 
13: ### What is Outcome-Driven Innovation (ODI)?
14: 
15: ODI is a strategy and innovation process rooted in the **Jobs-to-be-Done (JTBD)** theory. Its core premise is: **people buy products and services to get a "job" done**. A "job" is the functional process a person is trying to execute — it remains stable over time, while products and technologies are point-in-time solutions that eventually become obsolete.
16: 
17: ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.
18: 
19: ---
20: 
21: ### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done
22: 
23: - A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
24: - A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
25: - **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
26: - ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.
27: 
28: ---
29: 
30: ### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes
31: 
32: - **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
33: - Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
34: - **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):
35: 
36:   > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`
37: 
38:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
39:   - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
40:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
41:   - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.
42: 
43: - **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.
44: 
45: ---
46: 
47: ### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)
48: 
49: - All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
50:   1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
51:   2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
52:   3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
53:   4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
54:   5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
55:   6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
56:   7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
57:   8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs
58: 
59: - **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
60: - ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.
61: 
62: ---
63: 
64: ### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)
65: 
66: - Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
67:   - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
68:   - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?
69: 
70: - **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):
71: 
72:   ```
73:   Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
74:   ```
75: 
76: - **Interpretation**:
77:   - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
78:   - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
79:   - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.

ODI achieves an **86% innovation success rate** by replacing guesswork with a rigorous, data-driven framework grounded in measurable customer needs.

---

### Stage 1: Define the Market and the Job-to-be-Done

- A **market** is defined as: **a group of people + the functional job they are trying to get done** (e.g., "parents trying to pass on life lessons to children").
- A **Job-to-be-Done** is the core functional unit of analysis. It is NOT a product, solution, or feature — it is a stable human goal.
- **Agent rule**: Before anything else, the agent MUST help the user define the Job-to-be-Done. If no Job exists, use `add_job` to capture it. If one exists already, use `get_jobs()` to check first.
- ❌ **Never skip this stage**. No outcomes, steps, or scoring can be meaningful without a well-defined Job.

---

### Stage 2: Uncover Desired Outcomes

- **Desired outcomes** are the metrics customers use to measure success when getting a job done. They are the "needs" in ODI.
- Qualitative interviews typically uncover **50–150 desired outcome statements**.
- **Correct outcome statement format** (must be enforced when capturing user input):

  > `[Direction] + [Unit of Measure] + [Object of Control] + [Contextual Clarifier]`

  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the time it takes to determine if the corn seeds are germinating."*
  - ✅ **Good**: *"Minimize the likelihood of damaging the surface when cutting."*
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"Make it faster"* — too vague, no direction, no measurable unit.
  - ❌ **Bad**: *"I want a notification"* — this is a solution/feature, not an outcome.

- **Agent rule**: Guide the user to express outcomes using this exact format. Reject or reframe vague statements before calling `add_outcome`. Always capture `importance` and `satisfaction` scores (1–10 scale) to enable opportunity scoring.

---

### Stage 3: Inventory the Job (Universal Job Map)

- All functional jobs decompose into **8 universal process steps** (the Universal Job Map):
  1. **Define** — Plan what needs to be done; select goals or resources
  2. **Locate** — Gather the inputs, information, or resources needed
  3. **Prepare** — Set up and organize everything required
  4. **Confirm** — Validate readiness; decide whether to proceed
  5. **Execute** — Perform the core task
  6. **Monitor** — Verify and track performance while executing
  7. **Modify** — Adjust or update based on feedback
  8. **Conclude** — Store, finish, or dispose of outputs

- **Agent rule**: When a user is decomposing a job into steps, reference these 8 universal stages as a guide. Steps captured via `add_step` should map to or be inspired by these universal phases. Use `get_job_map` to visualize the ordered structure.
- ❌ **Do not build the Job Map before capturing outcome statements** — outcomes define *what success looks like*; the job map defines *where in the process* that success matters.

---

### Stage 4: Discover Where the Market is Underserved (Opportunity Scoring)

- Each desired outcome is rated by customers on two dimensions:
  - **Importance** (1–10): How important is this outcome to the customer?
  - **Satisfaction** (1–10): How satisfied are customers with current solutions?

- **Opportunity Algorithm** (must be implemented correctly):

  ```
  Opportunity Score = Importance + Max(Importance - Satisfaction, 0)
  ```

- **Interpretation**:
  - **Score > 10**: Underserved need — significant innovation opportunity.
  - **Score 10**: Appropriately served — maintain, don't over-invest.
  - **Score < 10**: Overserved — potential for disruption via lower-cost alternatives.

# Testing

## Commands

```bash
uv run pytest                       # all packages + root contract/launcher tests
uv run pytest packages/core         # one package
uv run pytest tests/contract        # MCP contract only
uv run mypy apps packages tests
uv run ruff check .
uv run ruff format --check .
uv run bandit -c pyproject.toml -r apps packages
```

The root `pyproject.toml` owns pytest, coverage, ruff, mypy, and bandit configuration. There is no per-package test configuration to keep in sync.

## Layout

Tests live next to their package (`packages/*/tests`, `apps/*/tests`). Root `tests/` contains only cross-package checks:

- `tests/contract/test_mcp_contract.py` — live FastMCP names, argument names, and required fields match `agentic_odi_core.contract.TOOL_SPECS`.
- `tests/contract/test_cli_contract.py` — the CLI local-handler keys are a subset of `TOOL_NAMES`.
- `tests/scripts/` — dev launcher helpers and lifecycle.

## Isolation Rules

- Use `InMemoryRepository` in tests. `create_app(InMemoryRepository())` keeps the Studio API off the real `~/.agentic-odi/odi.db`.
- The MCP server uses `build_repository()`; tests set `AGENTIC_ODI_DB=:memory:` before import and call tools through `Client(mcp)` without HTTP.
- Async tests use `@pytest.mark.asyncio` (strict mode).

CI runs the root suite on Python 3.10, 3.11, and 3.12, collects coverage for every `agentic_odi_*` distribution, and uploads `coverage.xml` from the 3.12 job. <skill_content name="writing-plans">
# Skill: writing-plans

# Writing Plans

## Overview

Write implementation plans for an engineer who has not seen this codebase or this spec. Assume they write idiomatic code in the project's language once they know the exact interface and the exact test, and that they will make a reasonable choice wherever the plan leaves one open. What they cannot know is what you decided: which files, which names and signatures, which values from the spec, which tests prove each task. Document those. Give them the whole plan as bite-sized tasks. DRY. YAGNI. TDD. Frequent commits.

**Announce at start:** "I'm using the writing-plans skill to create the implementation plan."

**Context:** If working in an isolated worktree, it should have been created via the `superpowers:using-git-worktrees` skill at execution time.

**Save plans to:** `docs/superpowers/plans/YYYY-MM-DD-<feature-name>.md`
- (User preferences for plan location override this default)

## Scope Check

If the spec covers multiple independent subsystems, it should have been broken into sub-project specs during brainstorming. If it wasn't, suggest breaking this into separate plans — one per subsystem. Each plan should produce working, testable software on its own.

## File Structure

Before defining tasks, map out which files will be created or modified and what each one is responsible for. This is where decomposition decisions get locked in.

- Design units with clear boundaries and well-defined interfaces. Each file should have one clear responsibility.
- You reason best about code you can hold in context at once, and your edits are more reliable when files are focused. Prefer smaller, focused files over large ones that do too much.
- Files that change together should live together. Split by responsibility, not by technical layer.
- In existing codebases, follow established patterns. If the codebase uses large files, don't unilaterally restructure - but if a file you're modifying has grown unwieldy, including a split in the plan is reasonable.

This structure informs the task decomposition. Each task should produce self-contained changes that make sense independently.

## Task Right-Sizing

A task is the smallest unit that carries its own test cycle and is worth a
fresh reviewer's gate. When drawing task boundaries: fold setup,
configuration, scaffolding, and documentation steps into the task whose
deliverable needs them; split only where a reviewer could meaningfully
reject one task while approving its neighbor. Each task ends with an
independently testable deliverable.

## Step Granularity

**Each step is one action with a checkable result:**
- "Write the failing test" - step
- "Run it to make sure it fails" - step
- "Implement the minimal code to make the test pass" - step
- "Run the tests and make sure they pass" - step
- "Commit" - step

## Plan Document Header

**Every plan MUST start with this header:**

```markdown
# [Feature Name] Implementation Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development (recommended) or superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** [One sentence describing what this builds]

**Architecture:** [2-3 sentences about approach]

**Tech Stack:** [Key technologies/libraries]

**Spec:** [path to the spec/design doc this plan implements — the plan
argues from the spec, so the spec travels with it; executors read both]

## Global Constraints

[The spec's project-wide requirements — version floors, dependency limits,
naming and copy rules, platform requirements — one line each, with exact
values copied verbatim from the spec. Every task's requirements implicitly
include this section.]

## Review Focus

[The five input classes or failure modes the spec implies but no task's
tests exercise that are most likely to bite a person using this software
— one line each, naming the input or condition and the behavior a
reasonable person would expect, most likely first. The spec is a vision
document: it says what the software must do, not everything it will
meet, and its silence on an input is not permission for that input to
break the program. Write the list here, once, with the spec in front of
you. Then, for each line, add the test that pins it to the task that
owns the code, in that task's own step style.]

---
```

## Task Structure

````markdown
### Task N: [Component Name]

**Files:**
- Create: `exact/path/to/file.py`
- Modify: `exact/path/to/existing.py:123-145`
- Test: `tests/exact/path/to/test.py`

**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: [what this task uses from earlier tasks — exact signatures]
- Produces: [what later tasks rely on — exact function names, parameter
  and return types. A task's implementer sees only their own task; this
  block is how they learn the names and types neighboring tasks use.]

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test**

```python
def test_specific_behavior():
    result = function(input)
    assert result == expected
```

- [ ] **Step 2: Run test to verify it fails**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: FAIL with "function not defined"

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement `function(input: InputType) -> ResultType` in `exact/path/to/file.py`**

One line on the approach when the signature and the test leave a choice
(which library call, which data structure); a code block only for an
algorithm they do not determine.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run test to verify it passes**

Run: `pytest tests/path/test.py::test_name -v`
Expected: PASS

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit**

```bash
git add tests/path/test.py src/path/file.py
git commit -m "feat: add specific feature"
```
````

## What a Step Contains

A step is done when the implementer can write exactly one reasonable thing
from it. That is the whole requirement: unambiguous, not complete. Each kind
of step carries what makes it unambiguous and nothing more:

- **A test step:** the test's name and its assertions, as code, with the
  spec's exact values in them.
- **A code step:** the exact signature (name, parameters, return type), the
  file it lives in, and the specific values the spec pins. The implementer
  writes the body. A body appears only for an algorithm the signature and
  tests do not determine, or for exact copy the spec fixes.
- **A verification step:** the command to run and the output that means it
  passed.
- **A reference to another task:** that task's Interfaces block says what
  to use; the plan does not repeat that task's code.

A plan is the set of decisions the implementer cannot make alone. A plan
longer than the code it describes has written the code instead. Lines that
decide nothing ("TBD", "handle edge cases", "add appropriate validation",
"write tests for the above", a type or function no task defines) are the
opposite failure, and the self-review catches both.

## Self-Review

After writing the complete plan, look at the spec with fresh eyes and check the plan against it. This is a checklist you run yourself — not a subagent dispatch.

**1. Spec coverage:** Skim each section/requirement in the spec. Can you point to a task that implements it? List any gaps.

**2. Step scan:** Every step must let the implementer write exactly one reasonable thing, and no step may carry more than that: a line that decides nothing is a gap, a function body the signature and tests already determine is a transcript. Fix both.

**3. Type consistency:** Do the types, method signatures, and property names you used in later tasks match what you defined in earlier tasks? A function called `clearLayers()` in Task 3 but `clearFullLayers()` in Task 7 is a bug.

**4. Review Focus:** For each input class or failure mode the spec implies, is there a task whose tests exercise it? The five uncovered ones most likely to bite a person go in the Review Focus section, and each line there gets its test added to the owning task. An empty section means you checked and found none, not that you skipped the check.

**5. Proportion:** Compare the plan's length to the spec's. A plan several times longer than the spec it implements is a transcript of the program, not a plan. If code blocks are most of the document, replace bodies with signatures, test names and assertions, and check that each step is still unambiguous.

If you find issues, fix them inline. No need to re-review — just fix and move on. If you find a spec requirement with no task, add the task.

## Execution Handoff

After saving and self-reviewing the plan, link it for your human partner
to read. If they have already explicitly supplied an execution method, ask
them to review the plan and confirm it captures what they want; wait for that
review before implementation, then use the preserved method. Otherwise, ask
them to review the plan and choose an execution method before implementation.

**When no execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Which execution approach would you prefer?**

- **Subagent-driven** - A fresh subagent implements each task and a fresh reviewer checks it before the next one starts, then a whole-branch review at the end. Most thorough; costs a fresh context per task and per review.
- **Native** - I implement every task myself in this session, the way this harness runs work, then one fresh reviewer on the most capable model checks the whole branch. Cheapest and fastest; no independent review until the end. Runs well with a mid-tier session model, since the plan carries the design.

**For this plan I recommend <one of the two>, because <one sentence from the plan: how much the tasks depend on each other's interfaces, how many there are, what a shipped mistake would cost>. Does the plan capture what you want, and which approach should we use?"**

**When an execution method has already been supplied:**

**"Plan complete and saved to `docs/superpowers/plans/<filename>.md`. Please review the plan. Does it capture what you want?"**

**If Subagent-driven chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:subagent-driven-development

**If Native chosen:**
- **REQUIRED SUB-SKILL:** Use superpowers:executing-plans

Base directory for this skill: /home/alexa/repos/agentic-odi/repos/agentic-odi/ui-not-looking-like-shit/.agents/skills/writing-plans
Relative paths in this skill (e.g., scripts/, reference/) are relative to this base directory.

# Max Studio Assistant-UI Integration Plan

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Bring the `ui-not-looking-like-shit` branch to the full "max" assistant-ui integration represented by `feat/studio-assistant-ui-existence` — adding backend approval gates, conversation branching, reasoning/source/tool-part streaming, and a complete frontend `assistant/` module with runtime provider, rich message conversion, part rendering, and attachment adapters.

**Architecture:** Adopt the reference branch's approach wholesale: an `assistant/StudioRuntime.tsx` wraps the app with `AssistantRuntimeProvider`; `assistant/convert.ts` does bidirectional Studio↔assistant-ui message conversion with reasoning, sources, tool approvals, and attachments; `assistant/parts.tsx` renders each part kind; `ThreadComposer.tsx` replaces `Composer.tsx`; `StudioContext` gains branching and approval methods; the backend gains `approvals.py`, conversation tree memory, and event-stream reasoning/source/approval emission.

**Tech Stack:** FastAPI + SQLite (studio-api), React + TypeScript + `@assistant-ui/react@0.15.31` (studio SPA), Vitest + pytest.

**Spec:** `feat/studio-assistant-ui-experience` branch — the reference implementation. All file contents and test expectations are read from this branch.

## Global Constraints

- Keep `@assistant-ui/react@^0.15.31` (already pinned in `apps/studio/package.json`).
- Python 3.10+; async tests decorated with `@pytest.mark.asyncio`.
- Use `InMemoryRepository` + `create_app(InMemoryRepository())` in API tests; never touch real `~/.agentic-odi/studio.db`.
- Frontend: `npm --prefix apps/studio test -- --run` for Vitest; `npm --prefix apps/studio run typecheck` for tsc.
- All Python: `uv run ruff check .` and `uv run ruff format --check .` must pass.
- `uv run mypy apps packages` must pass.

## Review Focus

| Input / Condition | Expected Behavior |
|---|---|
| Assistant emits a `reasoning` delta in the SSE stream | Renders in `ReasoningPart`, hidden by default, expandable. |
| Assistant calls a write tool without `requires_approval` flag | No approval gate; tool runs directly. |
| Assistant calls a write tool with `requires_approval` flag | Stream emits `approval` event; turn pauses; UI shows approval prompt. |
| User accepts or declines approval | `PATCH /api/approvals/{id}` with `approved` + `reason`; turn resumes or ends. |
| User asks a follow-up question after a tool result | New turn has the tool result as a `source`; model sees full visible history. |
| Image attachment > 5 MB | Rejected client-side with human-readable message. |
| Legacy conversation rows (no `message_id`/`parent_id`) | Read as a linear chain; head = last row. |
| User switches branches | Head updates; subsequent turns branch from the selected ancestor. |
| `content` field arrives on a part we don't map | Dropped; other parts preserved for history. |

---

Tasks are ordered by dependency: **Backend first** (API, schemas, memory, approvals), then **Frontend types**, then **Frontend assistant module**, then **Component wiring**, then **Tests**, finally **Docs**.

```python
class ApprovalRequest(BaseModel):
    id: str
    tool_call_id: str
    name: str
    arguments: dict[str, Any]
    prompt: str

class ApprovalDecision(BaseModel):
    approved: bool
    reason: str

class ApprovalNotFoundError(Exception): ...

class ApprovalRegistry:
    def __init__(self) -> None: ...
    @property
    def pending(self) -> int: ...
    def open(self, tool_call_id, name, arguments, prompt) -> tuple[ApprovalRequest, asyncio.Future]: ...
    def resolve(self, id, decision: ApprovalDecision) -> ApprovalRequest: ...
    def get(self, id) -> ApprovalRequest: ...
    async def wait_for_decision(self, id) -> ApprovalDecision: ...
    def cancel(self, id) -> None: ...
```

> **For agentic workers:** REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (`- [ ]`) syntax for tracking.

**Goal:** Bring the `ui-not-looking-like-shit` branch to the full "max" assistant-ui integration represented by `feat/studio-assistant-ui-experience` — adding backend approval gates, conversation branching, reasoning/source/tool-part streaming, and a complete frontend `assistant/` module with runtime provider, rich message conversion, part rendering, and attachment adapters.

**Architecture:** Adopt the reference branch's approach wholesale: an `assistant/StudioRuntime.tsx` wraps the app with `AssistantRuntimeProvider`; `assistant/convert.ts` does bidirectional Studio↔assistant-ui message conversion with reasoning, sources, tool approvals, and attachments; `assistant/parts.tsx` renders each part kind; `ThreadComposer.tsx` replaces `Composer.tsx`; `StudioContext` gains branching and approval methods; the backend gains `approvals.py`, conversation tree memory, and event-stream reasoning/source/approval emission.

**Tech Stack:** FastAPI + SQLite (studio-api), React + TypeScript + `@assistant-ui/react@0.15.31` (studio SPA), Vitest + pytest.

**Spec:** `feat/studio-assistant-ui-experience` branch — the reference implementation. All file contents and test expectations are read from this branch.

## Review Focus

| Input / Condition | Expected Behavior |
|---|---|
| Assistant emits a `reasoning` delta in the SSE stream | Renders in `ReasoningPart`, hidden by default, expandable. |
| Assistant calls a write tool without `requires_approval` flag | No approval gate; tool runs directly. |
| Assistant calls a write tool with `requires_approval` flag | Stream emits `approval` event; turn pauses; UI shows approval prompt. |
| User accepts or declines approval | `PATCH /api/approvals/{id}` with `approved` + `reason`; turn resumes or ends. |
| User asks a follow-up question after a tool result | New turn has the tool result as a `source`; model sees full visible history. |
| Image attachment > 5 MB | Rejected client-side with human-readable message. |
| Legacy conversation rows (no `message_id`/`parent_id`) | Read as a linear chain; head = last row. |
| User switches branches | Head updates; subsequent turns branch from the selected ancestor. |
| `content` field arrives on a part we don't map | Dropped; other parts preserved for history. |

+"""In-process approval gates for mutating tool calls.
+
+A mutating MCP tool (``add_job``, ``update_outcome``, …) pauses the streaming
+turn until the person in front of the Studio says yes or no. The gate is a
+process-local registry of pending futures: the SSE generator awaits one, and
+``POST /api/approvals/{id}`` resolves it.
+
+This is deliberately the smallest thing that is honest. The sidecar serves one
+local user over one loopback socket; it has no durable job state and no worker
+pool, so a gate that lives in memory is the whole requirement. Every gate has a
+timeout and every gate resolves once, so a turn can never hang and a double
+click can never run a tool twice.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import asyncio
+import threading
+import uuid
+from dataclasses import dataclass, field
+from datetime import datetime, timezone
+
+#: A person deciding whether the agent may write to their data deserves longer
+#: than a network timeout, but the turn must still end on its own.
+DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300.0
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ApprovalRequest:
+    """One pending decision, described well enough for the UI to ask."""
+
+    id: str
+    tool_call_id: str
+    name: str
+    arguments: dict[str, object]
+    prompt: str
+    created_at: str = field(default_factory=lambda: datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat())
+
+    def to_dict(self) -> dict[str, object]:
+        return {
+            "id": self.id,
+            "tool_call_id": self.tool_call_id,
+            "name": self.name,
+            "arguments": self.arguments,
+            "prompt": self.prompt,
+            "created_at": self.created_at,
+        }
+
+
+@dataclass
+class ApprovalDecision:
+    approved: bool
+    reason: str = ""
+
+
+class ApprovalNotFoundError(KeyError):
+    """No pending gate has that id, or it already resolved."""
+
+
+class ApprovalRegistry:
+    """Pending approval gates, keyed by the id the client answers with."""
+
+    def __init__(self) -> None:
+        self._lock = threading.Lock()
+        self._pending: dict[str, asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision]] = {}
+
+    def open(
+        self,
+        *,
+        tool_call_id: str,
+        name: str,
+        arguments: dict[str, object],
+        prompt: str,
+    ) -> tuple[ApprovalRequest, asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision]]:
+        """Register a gate and return its description and the future to await."""
+        loop = asyncio.get_running_loop()
+        request = ApprovalRequest(
+            id=f"apv_{uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]}",
+            tool_call_id=tool_call_id,
+            name=name,
+            arguments=arguments,
+            prompt=prompt,
+        )
+        future: asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision] = loop.create_future()
+        with self._lock:
+            self._pending[request.id] = future
+        return request, future
+
+    def resolve(self, approval_id: str, decision: ApprovalDecision) -> None:
+        """Answer a pending gate. Raises when the gate is unknown or already closed."""
+        with self._lock:
+            future = self._pending.pop(approval_id, None)
+        if future is None or future.done():
+            raise ApprovalNotFoundError(approval_id)
+        future.set_result(decision)
+
+    def discard(self, approval_id: str) -> None:
+        """Forget a gate without answering it (the turn ended first)."""
+        with self._lock:
+            self._pending.pop(approval_id, None)
+
+    def cancel_all(self) -> None:
+        """Drop every pending gate. Called when the sidecar shuts down."""
+        with self._lock:
+            pending = list(self._pending.items())
+            self._pending.clear()
+        for _approval_id, future in pending:
+            if not future.done():
+                future.cancel()
+
+    @property
+    def pending(self) -> int:
+        with self._lock:
+            return len(self._pending)
+
+
+async def wait_for_decision(
+    registry: ApprovalRegistry,
+    request: ApprovalRequest,
+    future: asyncio.Future[ApprovalDecision],
+    timeout: float = DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS,
+) -> ApprovalDecision | None:
+    """Await a decision, returning ``None`` when the gate expired or was dropped.
+
+    The gate is always discarded, so an expired id can never be answered later
+    and a cancelled turn leaves nothing behind.
+    """
+    try:
+        return await asyncio.wait_for(future, timeout=timeout)
+    except asyncio.TimeoutError:
+        return None
+    except asyncio.CancelledError:
+        raise
+    finally:
+        registry.discard(request.id)
+
+
+__all__ = [
+    "ApprovalDecision",
+    "ApprovalNotFoundError",
+    "ApprovalRegistry",
+    "ApprovalRequest",
+    "DEFAULT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS",
+    "wait_for_decision",
+]

+    reasoning = "reasoning"

+"""The write-approval gate: it resolves once, expires, and never leaks."""

+def _open(registry: ApprovalRegistry) -> tuple[object, object]:
+    async def _run() -> tuple[object, object]:
+        return registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1",
+            name="add_job",
+            arguments={"name": "Retention"},
+            prompt="Allow the assistant to add job?",
+        )
+
+    return asyncio.run(_run())
+
+
+def test_open_describes_the_call_for_the_ui() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+    request, _future = _open(registry)
+
+    payload = request.to_dict()  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+
+    assert payload["id"].startswith("apv_")
+    assert payload["tool_call_id"] == "call-1"
+    assert payload["name"] == "add_job"
+    assert payload["arguments"] == {"name": "Retention"}
+    assert payload["prompt"] == "Allow the assistant to add job?"
+    assert registry.pending == 1
+
+
+def test_resolve_answers_the_waiting_turn() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> ApprovalDecision:
+        request, future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        pending = asyncio.create_task(wait_for_decision(registry, request, future, timeout=5))
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        registry.resolve(request.id, ApprovalDecision(approved=True, reason="ok"))
+        decision = await pending
+        assert decision is not None
+        return decision
+
+    decision = asyncio.run(_run())
+
+    assert decision.approved is True
+    assert decision.reason == "ok"
+    assert registry.pending == 0
+
+
+def test_an_expired_gate_returns_none_and_is_forgotten() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> ApprovalDecision | None:
+        request, future = registry.open(
+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )
+        return await wait_for_decision(registry, request, future, timeout=0.01)
+
+    assert asyncio.run(_run()) is None
+    assert registry.pending == 0
+
+
+def test_a_gate_answers_only_once() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> None:
+        request, future = registry.open(

+        )
+        registry.resolve(request.id, ApprovalDecision(approved=True))
+        with pytest.raises(ApprovalNotFoundError):
+            registry.resolve(request.id, ApprovalDecision(approved=False))
+        await asyncio.sleep(0)
+        assert future.done()
+
+    asyncio.run(_run())
+
+
+def test_an_unknown_gate_cannot_be_resolved() -> None:

+
+    with pytest.raises(ApprovalNotFoundError):

+

+def test_cancel_all_drops_every_pending_gate() -> None:
+    registry = ApprovalRegistry()
+
+    async def _run() -> list[bool]:

+            tool_call_id="call-1", name="add_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
+        )

+            tool_call_id="call-2", name="delete_job", arguments={}, prompt="?"
